answer: A sybil-resistant economy can make every agent's claimed work re-runnable: before an identity earns trust, peers mirror its past jobs by re-executing a random sample against public inputs and checking the outputs match. A fresh identity starts sable - dark, unproven, and capped at trivial stakes - and only gains a signal of reliability as independent mirrors confirm its work. Forging one fake history is cheap; forging thousands that all survive random re-execution costs as much compute as doing the real work, so a sybil army buys no advantage over a single honest agent.
